name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q09 - Sedimentation profile of DNA ligase mutant replication

questiontext.text: Replication was allowed to take place in the presence of radioactive deoxynucleotides precursors in E. coli that was a mutant for DNA ligase. Newly synthesised radioactive DNA was purified and strands were separated by denaturation. These were centrifuged using density gradient centrifugation. Which of the following would be a correct result?

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions
Replication is conducted in a mutant strain of Escherichia coli lacking functional DNA ligase.
Radioactive deoxynucleotide precursors are present during synthesis, incorporating radioactivity into nascent DNA.
Newly synthesized DNA is purified, denatured into single strands, and separated by density gradient centrifugation according to molecular weight.

Assumptions and Sign Conventions
DNA replication is semiconservative and semi-discontinuous.
High molecular weight corresponds to long, continuous polynucleotide strands.
Low molecular weight corresponds to short, unjoined Okazaki fragments.

Relevant Formulae and Principles
DNA-dependent DNA polymerase synthesizes DNA exclusively in the 5' to 3' direction.
The leading strand is synthesized continuously, producing full-length, high-molecular-weight DNA.
The lagging strand is synthesized discontinuously as short Okazaki fragments.
DNA ligase is specifically required to form phosphodiester bonds that link adjacent Okazaki fragments into an unbroken high-molecular-weight strand.

Step-by-Step Working
Continuous synthesis along the leading strand proceeds uninterrupted, incorporating radioactive precursors to form full-length, high-molecular-weight radioactive strands.
On the lagging strand, Okazaki fragments are synthesized with radioactive precursors; however, because the cell lacks functional DNA ligase, these fragments cannot be covalently joined together.
Upon denaturation into single strands, the high-molecular-weight leading strands separate from the low-molecular-weight Okazaki fragments.
Centrifugation in a density gradient separates these two size classes into two distinct zones: one representing high-molecular-weight continuous strands and the other representing low-molecular-weight unjoined fragments.

Check and Final Answer
Because one strand is continuous and the other remains entirely fragmented, radioactivity is distributed between two distinct molecular weight fractions. The correct sedimentation profile exhibits two distinct radioactivity peaks: one at high molecular weight and another at low molecular weight.
